source.title: Towards Evaluation for Real-World LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Kehao Miao; Yu-Ke Hu; Xiaochen Li; Wenjie Bao; Zhi-Hao Liu; Zhan Qin; Kui Ren

page_placements.theme: Unlearned models stay near the original and distinguishable from a retrained model (non-MIA traces)

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper applies its own evaluation metric to several unlearning methods and concludes that their results indicate incomplete forgetting. This challenges claims of complete unlearning, but it does not measure the attack outcomes or behavioral accuracy specified in versions A–F.
record.gate_note: Table 3 reports DCUE scores for unlearned models and reference models; these are recorded below as findings about target-knowledge confidence, not as accuracy or recovery-attack results. The paper also reports comparisons among evaluation metrics and DCUE approximation/ablation results, which do not measure recovery of the targeted knowledge and are omitted. The prompts in the paper are extraction-prompt examples, not instructions addressed to an AI reading or reviewing the paper.
record.test_reason: The study proposes the DCUE metric and applies it to six unlearning methods on a modified TOFU set of fictitious-author QA pairs. It reports no forget-set accuracy, no general-ability check and no recovery attack (fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization or prompting) on unlearned models. DCUE is a KS-test p-value. It compares the core-token confidence distribution on the forget set with a corrected original model that stands in for the retrained model. A low score only says the distribution differs from the retrained proxy. It cannot say whether knowledge is retained, suppressed or over-forgotten. The study also does not examine whether access is blocked rather than the knowledge deleted. This is a related but different construct (a confidence-distribution score, not the behaviour a version names), so it is recorded under fits_no_version and gets no verdict on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is correct in substance. The authors also claim DCUE beats existing metrics on practicality, exactness and robustness (Table 2; Table 4 in Appendix C adds Qwen2.5-7B and MUSE-News). They say their finding of incomplete unlearning agrees with other studies: quantization recovery (Zhang et al.), targeted relearning (Hu et al.) and Lynch et al.'s robustness evaluations. They do not run those attacks themselves.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes DCUE as an evaluation metric and applies it to existing methods; it does not reproduce the original recovery attacks or methods named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported DCUE outcomes vary with model and forget fraction (2%, 10%, and 20%).

fits_no_version.finding: On DCUE (KS p-value of core-token confidence against a corrected original model), all six methods (GA, GD, IDK, DPO, NPO, SimNPO) on Phi-1.5B and LLaMA2-7B score at most 8.02e-05. The retrained Mr scores 0.90-1.0. This holds at 2%, 10% and 20% forget fractions. Relative to Mt, scores range from 0.84x (GA, Phi, 2%) to 6.9e8x (SimNPO, LLaMA, 20%), so the gap to Mt grows with forget fraction but stays many orders of magnitude below Mr. SimNPO ranks best and GA second.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient- and preference-based unlearning of fine-tuned QA data leaves the forget-set core-token confidence distribution far from that of a retrained model, as measured by DCUE.

record.problems: The evidence on residual knowledge uses DCUE core-token confidence distributions rather than behavioral accuracy or direct recovery attacks. The text reports no uncertainty estimates for Table 3 results.
record.rows_left_out: None from Table 3; all reported model × method × forget-fraction DCUE values and the Mt/Mr references are included.

untested.parts: None of these is measured: forget-set accuracy near chance, preserved general ability, or simple attacks failing to recover the knowledge.
Recovery by relearning fine-tuning. Fine-tuning on unrelated data (PostPro_ft) appears only as a metric-robustness test applied to Mr, not as an attack on unlearned models.
No activation ablation and no analysis of blocking versus deletion.
No recovery by prompting or jailbreaks. Jailbreak-style questions are used only to build an existing text-similarity metric (AA) for the metric comparison in Table 2.
No method that claims to resist attacks is tested.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) Its row_fixes item for 'r1, r3, r5, r7, r9, r11' was refused as an unknown row id. I split it into six single-row items with the same judgment (the note mislabels Mt).
(2) The earlier verdict had two range items for 'r13-r48'. I expanded them into 36 single-row items and merged the two problems, so each row has one item. I reworded the 'of Dr' remark: the fraction most likely means a share of the fine-tuning set Dt.
(3) For r19-r24 I added that GD here is gradient difference, not plain gradient descent (Appendix D.2).
(4) The fits_no_version finding now gives the actual ranges: Mr 0.90-1.0, unlearned at most 8.02e-05, ratios to Mt from 0.84x to 6.9e8x. The earlier text said 'near Mt' and 'about 1.0'.
(5) I corrected the earlier note that Mr is used 'only in Table 3'. Mr is also used in the approximation check (Section 4.5, Figure 5) and as Mu for exactness+ and robustness in Table 2.

Kept: relation discusses, tranche T6, all six versions untested, no labels, missing empty. All 48 row values match Table 3.

Caveats:
- DCUE is a two-sided distribution distance, so a low p-value is also consistent with over-suppression of target-token probabilities rather than retention. No accuracy is reported to tell these apart.
- No uncertainty is reported for Table 3.
- Table 3 does not name its dataset. Section 5.1 says the experiments use a modified TOFU set.

The paper contains prompt templates for core-token extraction and for generating jailbreak questions. These are the study's materials, not instructions to the reader, and were ignored. No original source is involved: this study is not one of the three originals.

versions.untested_parts: Near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy, general ability, and whether simple attacks recover the knowledge.
Recovery after fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
Recovery by activation-direction ablation, or evidence that access is blocked rather than knowledge deleted.
Recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Whether a newer method resists the listed attacks.

relation.reason: Proposes a metric, applies it to six methods, and links its finding of incomplete unlearning to other work. It tests no version.

tranche.reason: DCUE is a KS p-value on core-token confidence distributions, a different construct from forget-set accuracy or recovery. No recovery attack is run; robustness tests use Mr as Mu (Sec. 5.1). The authors only cite agreement with Zhang et al. [44] and Lynch et al. [25].

source_check.notes: Table 3 values for all 25 checked rows match the text. Mt row notes wrongly call Mt an unlearned-model reference; Mt is the model before unlearning. The paper never spells out GD; its Appendix D.2 description (raise forget loss, lower retain loss) matches gradient difference, not 'gradient descent' as the op says. Section 5.3 says unlearned scores are only slightly above Mt and far below Mr.
